title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Invite people and be invited, find your way through the days of a Pakistani wedding, give gifts and Eidi, and offer the right wish or blessing at weddings, Eid, birthdays and Independence Day.
intro:
A Pakistani wedding isn't one day, it's a season: **ڈھولکی**, **مہندی**, **نکاح**, **بارات**, **رخصتی**, **ولیمہ**. Add the two Eids, Chand Raat, 14 August and birthdays, and you'll spend a lot of the year at occasions where there's a right thing to say.

This unit gives you the vocabulary of the big days and two pieces of grammar that come up at all of them: **wishes and blessings** (اللہ آپ کو خوش **رکھے**، **اللہ کرے**…، **جیتے رہو**), and the friendly ways to say **be sure to…** (ضرور **آنا**، لانا **مت بھولنا**، کھانا کھا کر **جانا**).

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings
grammar.body:
Wishes describe what you hope *will* happen, so they use the **subjunctive** — the future without گا (کرے، دے، رکھے، ہو). You met a few in unit 18; at weddings and festivals you'll hear them non-stop.

**اللہ / خدا + subjunctive** — a blessing: اللہ آپ کو خوش **رکھے** 'may God keep you happy', اللہ جوڑی سلامت **رکھے** 'may God keep the couple together', اللہ تمہیں کامیاب **کرے**, خدا آپ کو لمبی عمر **دے**.

**اللہ کرے / خدا کرے (کہ)** + subjunctive — 'God grant that…', the everyday way to say **I really hope**: اللہ کرے تم پاس **ہو جاؤ** 'I really hope you pass', اللہ کرے کل بارش **نہ** ہو 'fingers crossed it doesn't rain tomorrow'. Negative wishes take **نہ**, not نہیں.

**… مبارک ہو** — 'may … be blessed' = congratulations. The ہو is the subjunctive of ہونا. Name the occasion: عید مبارک ہو, نیا سال مبارک ہو, and put the person in **کو**: آپ **کو** نیا گھر مبارک ہو. As a noun: **مبارک باد**: سالگرہ کی مبارک باد, سب نے مبارک باد دی.

**Blessings from elders** are imperatives: **جیتے رہو** (to a boy) / **جیتی رہو** (to a girl) 'live long', **خوش رہو** 'be happy', **سلامت رہو** 'stay safe'. Young people answer by lowering their head or saying شکریہ.

**Replies:** to مبارک → **خیر مبارک** or شکریہ، آپ کو بھی; to any blessing or prayer → **آمین**; to a lovely wish → **آپ کے منہ میں گھی شکر**.

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…': ضرور, the infinitive and 'don't forget'
grammar.body:
Invitations come with a string of friendly instructions. Here's how they're built.

**ضرور** 'definitely' turns any request into 'be sure to': **ضرور** آئیے 'do come', **ضرور** بتانا 'be sure to tell me'. It can also come after the verb for emphasis: آنا **ضرور**!

**The infinitive as a request for later.** With تم, the plain infinitive is a gentle instruction for the future — not right now: **آنا** 'come (when the time comes)', **بتانا** 'let me know', فون **کرنا** 'give me a call'. With آپ, use the **-یے گا** form instead: آئیے گا، بتائیے گا. Compare: **آؤ!** 'come (here, now)!' vs شادی پر **آنا** 'come to the wedding'.

**Don't forget:** infinitive + **مت بھولنا / نہ بھولنا** (to آپ: **نہ بھولیے گا**): لفافہ لانا **مت بھولنا**. Or simply a negative infinitive: دیر سے **نہیں آنا** 'don't be late'.

**You simply have to:** add **ہی**: آپ کو آنا **ہی** ہے, آنا **ہی** پڑے گا.

**Before you go:** **کر کے / کھا کر** 'having done' and **… کیے بغیر / کھائے بغیر** 'without doing': کھانا کھا کر جانا 'eat before you go', کھانا کھائے **بغیر** مت جانا 'don't leave without eating' — something every host will say.

culture:
**A Pakistani wedding** is a series of functions. **ڈھولکی** nights: women and girls of the family sing wedding songs to the drum, sometimes for a week. **مہندی**: yellow and green clothes, henna, choreographed dances by cousins and friends from both sides. **نکاح**: the marriage itself, a short religious ceremony with a maulvi and witnesses, often held at home or in a mosque or on the baraat day. **بارات**: the groom arrives with his family at a hall hosted by the bride's family; the bride wears red. **رخصتی**: the bride leaves her parents' home — the emotional high point, with a Qur'an held over her head. **ولیمہ**: the groom's family's reception, a day or two later. Invitation times are famously optimistic: a card that says 8 pm usually means dinner at eleven.

**Gifts:** guests give **سلامی** — cash in an envelope with your name on it — to the bride or groom (or their mother); close family give gold or clothes. **Eid ul-Fitr** starts with **چاند رات** (bangles, henna, last-minute shopping), then Eid prayers, **گلے ملنا** three times, **شیر خورمہ**, new clothes, visiting relatives and **عیدی** for children (adults ask for it as a joke). On **بڑی عید** families buy a goat or share a cow weeks ahead, and the meat is shared with relatives and the poor. **14 August** means green-and-white flags on every car and rooftop and fireworks at midnight. Birthdays with cake and parties are mostly an urban, younger habit. Christians in Pakistan celebrate **بڑا دن** (Christmas) and Hindus in Sindh celebrate Diwali and Holi; a simple **مبارک ہو** is always right.

lessons.title: Inviting and being invited

tip.title: Be sure to come: ضرور آنا
tip.body:
- With تم, the **infinitive** is a friendly request for later: شادی پر **آنا**, مجھے **بتانا**.
- Add **ضرور** for 'be sure to': **ضرور** آنا / آنا **ضرور**!
- Don't forget: infinitive + **مت بھولنا**. Don't do it: **نہیں** + infinitive: دیر سے **نہیں آنا**.
- With آپ, use **-یے گا**: تشریف لائیے گا.

tip.title: Which function, which day
tip.body:
- The order: **ڈھولکی** → **مہندی** → **نکاح** and **بارات** → **رخصتی** → **ولیمہ**.
- 'At the X' is X **پر** or X **میں**: مہندی **پر**, شادی **میں**.
- Masculine nouns in -ہ change before a postposition: ولیمہ → ولیمے **پر**.

lessons.title: Wishes and blessings

tip.title: May God…: اللہ آپ کو خوش رکھے
tip.body:
- Blessings use the **subjunctive** (no گا): اللہ آپ کو خوش **رکھے**, کامیاب **کرے**, صحت **دے**.
- **اللہ کرے** + subjunctive = 'I really hope': اللہ کرے موسم اچھا **ہو**.
- **مبارک ہو**: the ہو is subjunctive too. Reply **خیر مبارک**; to a blessing, **آمین**.

sentences.roman: sālgirah par kek kis ne kāṭā?
sentences.en: Who cut the birthday cake?

sentences.native: اللہ تمہیں ہر خوشی دے۔
sentences.roman: allāh tumheṃ har xushī de.
sentences.en: May God give you every happiness.

sentences.native: خدا کرے تم امتحان میں پاس ہو جاؤ۔
sentences.roman: xudā kare tum imtihān meṃ pās ho jā’o.
sentences.en: I really hope you pass the exam.

sentences.native: اللہ تم دونوں کو ہمیشہ ساتھ رکھے۔
sentences.roman: allāh tum donoṃ ko hamesha sāth rakhe.
sentences.en: May God keep you two together always.

sentences.native: دادی نے کہا، جیتی رہو بیٹی!
sentences.roman: dādī ne kahā, jītī raho beṭī!
sentences.en: Grandma said, "Bless you, my girl!"

sentences.native: آپ سب کو نیا سال مبارک ہو!
sentences.roman: āp sab ko nayā sāl mubārak ho!
sentences.en: Happy New Year, everyone!

sentences.native: سب نے دولہا کو مبارک باد دی۔
sentences.roman: sab ne dūlhā ko mubārak bād dī.
sentences.en: Everyone congratulated the groom.

lessons.title: Gifts, Eidi and Eid

tip.title: Eid manners
tip.body:
- Greet with **عید مبارک**; the answer is **خیر مبارک، آپ کو بھی**.
- After Eid prayers people **گلے ملتے ہیں**, usually three times.
- Elders give children **عیدی**; at weddings guests give **سلامی** in a **لفافہ** with their name on it.

new: آپ کو اور آپ کے گھر والوں کو عید مبارک۔

sentences.native: شادی پر کتنی سلامی دینی چاہیے؟
sentences.roman: shādī par kitnī salāmī denī chāhiye?
sentences.en: How much should you give as a wedding gift?

sentences.native: لفافے پر اپنا نام لکھ دینا۔
sentences.roman: lifāfe par apnā nām likh denā.
sentences.en: Write your name on the envelope.

sentences.native: ماموں نے مجھے پانچ ہزار عیدی دی!
sentences.roman: māmūṃ ne mujhe pāṃch hazār ʿīdī dī!
sentences.en: My uncle gave me five thousand as Eidi!

sentences.native: بچوں کو سب سے زیادہ عیدی کا انتظار ہوتا ہے۔
sentences.roman: bachchoṃ ko sab se zyāda ʿīdī kā intizār hotā hai.
sentences.en: What the kids look forward to most is their Eidi.

sentences.native: چاند رات کو ہم چوڑیاں لینے بازار جائیں گے۔
sentences.roman: chāṃd rāt ko ham chūṛiyāṃ lene bāzār jā’eṃ ge.
sentences.en: On Chand Raat we'll go to the bazaar to get bangles.

sentences.native: امی ہر عید پر شیر خورمہ بناتی ہیں۔
sentences.roman: ammī har ʿīd par shīr xurma banātī haiṃ.
sentences.en: Mum makes sheer khurma every Eid.

sentences.native: عید کی نماز کے بعد سب ایک دوسرے سے گلے ملتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: ʿīd kī namāz ke baʿd sab ek dūsre se gale milte haiṃ.
sentences.en: After Eid prayers everyone embraces each other.

sentences.native: سلامی کا لفافہ دولہا کو دینا ہے یا اس کی امی کو؟
sentences.roman: salāmī kā lifāfa dūlhā ko denā hai yā us kī ammī ko?
sentences.en: Do I give the envelope to the groom or to his mum?

sentences.native: عید پر سب نئے کپڑے پہنتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: ʿīd par sab na’e kapṛe pahante haiṃ.
sentences.en: Everyone wears new clothes at Eid.

sentences.native: بڑی عید پر ہم قربانی کرتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: baṛī ʿīd par ham qurbānī karte haiṃ.
sentences.en: We do a sacrifice at Bari Eid.

sentences.native: بکرا کتنے کا لیا؟
sentences.roman: bakrā kitne kā liyā?
sentences.en: How much did you pay for the goat?

sentences.native: اس سال بکرے بہت مہنگے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: is sāl bakre bahut mahange haiṃ.
sentences.en: Goats are really expensive this year.

sentences.native: قربانی کا گوشت رشتہ داروں کو بھی بھیجا جاتا ہے۔
sentences.roman: qurbānī kā gosht rishta dāroṃ ko bhī bhejā jātā hai.
sentences.en: The sacrifice meat is sent to relatives too.

sentences.native: ہر طرف جھنڈے ہی جھنڈے ہیں!
sentences.roman: har taraf jhanḍe hī jhanḍe haiṃ!
sentences.en: There are flags everywhere!

sentences.native: گاڑی پر جھنڈا لگا لو!
sentences.roman: gāṛī par jhanḍā lagā lo!
sentences.en: Put a flag on the car!

sentences.native: آزادی کے دن بچے ہرے اور سفید کپڑے پہنتے ہیں۔
sentences.roman: āzādī ke din bachche hare aur safed kapṛe pahante haiṃ.
sentences.en: On Independence Day children wear green and white.

sentences.native: رات کو آتش بازی دیکھنے چلیں؟
sentences.roman: rāt ko ātish bāzī dekhne chaleṃ?
sentences.en: Shall we go and watch the fireworks tonight?

sentences.native: سب کو یوم آزادی مبارک!
sentences.roman: sab ko yaum-e āzādī mubārak!
sentences.en: Happy Independence Day, everyone!
